routes.label: Convert file size to kilobits, then seconds to minutes

question: When the World Wide Web first became popular in the 1990s, download speeds reached a maximum of about \(56\) kilobits per second. Approximately how many minutes would the download of a \(4.2\)-megabyte song have taken at that speed? (Note that there are \(8000\) kilobits in a megabyte.)
solution:
The file size and the download rate need matching units. Using the conversion given in the question, the song contains

\[
4.2\cdot8000=33{,}600
\]

kilobits. At \(56\) kilobits each second, downloading it takes

\[
\frac{33{,}600}{56}=600\text{ seconds}
=10\text{ minutes}.
\]

The answer is approximately \(\boxed{10}\) minutes, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
